findings.title: updateMany with empty data always throws
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 1024 fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma updateMany requires non-empty data and throws PrismaClientValidationError for {}. This runs after the cache upserts, so every cache warmup fails and watchCalendar/unwatchCalendar flows that call it will error.

findings.title: Delete cache does not invalidate calendar query
findings.body: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the deleteCache mutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess prop, while the disconnect mutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations. After deleting cache the cacheUpdatedAt value stays in the React Query cache, so the dropdown still shows the old timestamp and user thinks deletion failed until a full reload.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry
findings.body: In packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only considers rows with expiresAt >= now. Credentials with only expired rows will still report an updatedAt, causing the UI to show Cache Status and a Delete button for cache that will never be used.

findings.title: credentialId input allows floats and negatives
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx the deleteCache input is z.object({ credentialId: z.number() }). It accepts NaN, floats, zero and negatives. Prisma expects Int, so floats cause a Prisma validation 500 instead of a 400 input error. It should be z.number().int().positive().

findings.title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
findings.body: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh line 68 uses sed -i '' -E which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux sed interprets '' as a file name and fails, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for most contributors and CI. It needs OS detection or portable in-place edit handling.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcodes en-US locale
findings.body: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the cache last-updated timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...). This ignores the user's locale from useLocale, so non-US users see MM/DD dates inconsistent with the rest of the localized app.

findings.title: Unrelated dev:cron switch to npx tsx without dep
findings.body: In apps/web/package.json dev:cron was changed from ts-node to npx tsx unrelated to calendar cache. tsx is not in dependencies/devDependencies, so npx will fetch it on demand, breaking offline/hermetic installs and adding latency, while ts-node remains in devDependencies. It should be reverted or done in a separate PR with a declared dependency.
